meta.titre: Nigerian Nationalism and Independence: internal pressures, parties and leaders on the road to 1960
meta.sous_theme: Rise of nationalism in Nigeria after 1945 and the steps to independence

sections.contenu_markdown: Before 1960 Southern Cameroons was governed as part of British-ruled Nigeria, and even the name of a leading Nigerian party, the National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons, shows how close the two histories were. Nigeria became independent on 1 October 1960, after years of newspapers, strikes, new parties and constitutional talks. Examiners ask why nationalism grew after 1945 and how independence was reached. This course shows you the main forces inside Nigeria and a clear way of presenting them.

items: Nationalism is the wish of a people to rule themselves.
Nigeria was a British colony and protectorate.
A political party is a group that tries to win power through elections.

sections.titre: Nigerian nationalism after 1945: internal factors and the steps to 1960
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Internal factors behind the rise of nationalism after 1945

| Factor | How it helped nationalism |
|---|---|
| Educated elite | Nigerians educated in mission schools, at University College Ibadan (opened 1948) and abroad led the demand for self-rule |
| The press | Newspapers such as the West African Pilot spread nationalist ideas and criticised colonial rule |
| Ex-servicemen | Nigerian soldiers who had fought for Britain in the Second World War, in places such as Burma, came home with new ideas and found few rewards |
| Economic hardship | Rising prices after the war, low pay and marketing boards that paid farmers less than world prices caused anger |
| Labour unrest | A general strike in 1945 and the shooting of striking miners at Enugu in 1949 united workers against colonial rule |
| Political parties | The NCNC (formed in 1944), the Action Group and the Northern People's Congress organised people for self-government |
| Unpopular constitution | Many nationalists thought the Richards Constitution of 1946 gave Nigerians too little real power |

External factors, such as independence for India in 1947 and Ghana in 1957, also helped, but a question on internal factors asks only for the factors listed above.

### Main parties and leaders

| Party | Main region | Leaders |
|---|---|---|
| NCNC | East | Herbert Macaulay and Nnamdi Azikiwe |
| Action Group | West | Obafemi Awolowo |
| Northern People's Congress | North | Ahmadu Bello and Abubakar Tafawa Balewa |

### Steps to independence

The Richards Constitution (1946) was followed by the Macpherson Constitution (1951) and the Lyttelton Constitution (1954), which made Nigeria a federation. The Eastern and Western regions gained self-government in 1957 and the Northern region in 1959. Nigeria became independent on 1 October 1960 with Tafawa Balewa as prime minister.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks why nationalism grew inside the country
variantes.contenu_markdown: Choose only factors from inside Nigeria: the educated elite, the press, parties, trade unions, ex-servicemen, economic grievances. Explain each one. Leave out India, Ghana and the United Nations, which are external.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks for all the causes or compares the two groups
variantes.contenu_markdown: Present internal and external factors in two separate paragraphs and then judge which mattered more. Many historians stress the internal pressures because without organised Nigerian parties the external events would not have led to independence.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks how independence was achieved
variantes.contenu_markdown: Present the process in order: the Richards, Macpherson and Lyttelton constitutions, regional self-government and independence in 1960. Show that independence was reached by constitutional talks and negotiation, not by war.

sections.enonce_markdown: Explain how the activities of Nigerian political parties helped the struggle for independence. [6 marks]

etapes.justification: 'Explain how' needs actions and results, not only the names of the parties.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Aim: three activities, each linked to independence.

etapes.action: Plan around what the parties did.
etapes.justification: A plan focused on activities answers 'how'.
etapes.resultat_markdown: 1. Organised people. 2. Demanded constitutional change. 3. Took part in elections and talks.

etapes.justification: Facts such as dates and leaders gain the marks.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The NCNC, formed in 1944 under Macaulay and Azikiwe, held meetings and campaigns across the country and so created a mass movement.

etapes.justification: This shows how pressure produced change.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The parties criticised the Richards Constitution and pressed for changes, which led to the Macpherson and Lyttelton constitutions.

etapes.action: Develop the third activity and conclude.
etapes.justification: A conclusion answers the question as a whole.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Parties such as the Action Group and the NPC won elections in their regions, ran regional governments and took part in the talks that led to independence in 1960.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Model answer: Nigerian political parties helped the struggle for independence in three ways. First, they organised people. The NCNC, formed in 1944 under leaders such as Herbert Macaulay and Nnamdi Azikiwe, held meetings and campaigns across the country and created a mass movement for self-rule. Second, the parties demanded constitutional change. They criticised the Richards Constitution of 1946 and pressed Britain for reforms, which led to the Macpherson Constitution of 1951 and the Lyttelton Constitution of 1954. Third, the parties took part in elections and constitutional talks. The Action Group in the West and the Northern People's Congress in the North won power in their regions, gained experience of government and bargained with Britain until independence was granted in 1960. Therefore the parties turned a feeling of discontent into a political force.

items.pourquoi_faux: The year 1957 is the independence of Ghana. Nigeria became independent on 1 October 1960.
items.correction_markdown: Write 1960 for Nigeria and 1957 for Ghana.

items.erreur_markdown: Using the independence of India as an internal factor.
items.pourquoi_faux: India is outside Nigeria, so it is an external factor, and the question specifies internal ones.
items.correction_markdown: Write only about forces inside Nigeria: the elite, the press, parties, workers, ex-servicemen and economic grievances.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing that the three major parties covered the whole country equally.
items.pourquoi_faux: Each party had its main support in one region, and this regional split was a problem later.
items.correction_markdown: State the region of each party: NCNC in the East, Action Group in the West and NPC in the North.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing that Nigeria won its independence by fighting a war against Britain.
items.pourquoi_faux: Independence came through constitutional talks and pressure, not war.
items.correction_markdown: Write that Nigerian leaders used newspapers, strikes, elections and negotiations.

items.enonce_markdown: Name the three major political parties of Nigeria in the 1950s and the region each mainly served.
items.solution_markdown: The NCNC mainly served the **East**, the Action Group the **West** and the Northern People's Congress the **North**.

items.enonce_markdown: Explain how Nigerian soldiers who served in the Second World War contributed to the rise of nationalism.
items.solution_markdown: Award marks for: they fought for Britain in places such as Burma and met soldiers of other nations; they learned that Europeans were not superior; they came home with new ideas and skills; they found few rewards and little respect, which made them angry with colonial rule; they joined nationalist movements. **They returned with new ideas and grievances that strengthened nationalism.**

items.enonce_markdown: Which was more important in the rise of nationalism in Nigeria after 1945, internal or external factors? Give reasons. [8 marks]
items.solution_markdown: Award marks for internal factors: educated elite, press, parties, trade unions, economic grievances. Award marks for external factors: independence of India in 1947, the Second World War, the example of Ghana and the attitude of the United Nations. Credit a clear judgement, for example: **internal factors were more important, since organised Nigerian movements converted outside inspiration into action.**

items_markdown: Independence came on 1 October 1960, after constitutional talks and not war.
Internal factors after 1945: educated elite, press, ex-servicemen, economic hardship, strikes, parties and the unpopular Richards Constitution.
Main parties: NCNC in the East, Action Group in the West, Northern People's Congress in the North.
Constitutions: Richards 1946, Macpherson 1951, Lyttelton 1954, then regional self-government and independence.
Keep internal and external factors apart when the question names only one group.
Southern Cameroons was governed with Nigeria, so Nigerian politics affected Cameroon too.
